_comment: Per-subject curation for the ETG (Elite Temple Guard) unit-analysis video. The METHOD lives in code; this file holds only the ETG-specific choices, applied by build_v2_categorization.py.
_remove_note: The generic Battle Elephant staple is modal-Bengalis; the video uses the beefier Vietnamese Elite Battle Elephant instead (see extra_results).
_extra_results_note: These two were simmed separately (15 seeds, MAX_S=180) via a single-matchup V2 run rather than the batch. To re-sim them in the batch instead, move their keys into `add` and drop them here.
_ingame_note: V2 predicted a +10/80% ETG win for the Arambai, but 5 in-game runs were a 0/5 loss (S -72). Likewise V2 said ETG +41 vs the War Elephant, but the recorded fight was a decisive ETG loss (9 elephants wipe 21 ETG) — the trample + huge-HP blind spot. In-game ground truth wins; since ETG carries the anti-cav bonus, the War Elephant lands in UNEXPECTED LOSS. (White Feather Guard USED to be forced here too — V2 said +12/80% ETG win vs a 0/5 in-game ETG loss — but that was a real SIM BUG, now fixed: the no-SLOT model capped WFG's engaged units at frontage-parity with the ETG so its 21-vs-12 numerical edge was discarded. With the SLOT=4 envelopment fix in sim_v2_model.js the sim now flips to a 100% WFG win, so the override was removed — the sim earns the loss on its own. Arambai (ranged miss-graze) and War Elephant (trample) are orthogonal mechanics the envelopment fix does not address, so those overrides remain.)
_exclude_note: Genitour is never shown in the video (not a useful/representative unit); it still appears in the full table.
